chapter: Suntaug Lake Inn and Duke Ellington's band
title: Sacred concerts, conducting at Harvard and the first at Grace Cathedral
summary: Whaley tells how he rehearsed and conducted the choir at Harvard and Texas, and dates the first Sacred Concert in San Francisco.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: I could see Duke progressing every year it was something different and when he came into the sacred concert music, ah, that was my field. Oh, I loved --
I loved that voice, the choir and when
we was up at Harvard I got more applause than Duke or anybody in the band, anybody. When they'd call my name out, oh, them people would yell.
That's when they struck the Duke -- Are we talking about at Yale.
Harvard, when he played the Sacred Concert up there, see, I rehearsed it and the director up there he wouldn't direct it. He said you direct it and that's what the kids all liked.

Yeah, I conducted up there and I said, I got more applause than Duke or anybody. Oh, them kids really applaud and we went down Texas the same way. Some church down there had it and the man said, no, you know it, you direct it.
This was about in '65 or '66, somewhere around there. Let me see, the concerts started in '67, I think, his Sacred Concerts. The first one was out there in Grace Episcopal Church in San Francisco.
Then the rest of them must have been after this, '67 and '68 and '69. If this first on was in '67, the rest must have followed. Let me think.
Let me see, I think it was in '67 or '68, that first one was at Grace Episcopal. Oh, that place was crowded.
That's a matter of record, we could find that out very easy.
